highlights.title: Microsoft’s DLSS competitor is out for the Xbox Ally X and works in handheld mode
highlights.summary: Microsoft is now rolling out Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), an upscaling technology that competes with Nvidia's DLSS, for the Xbox Ally X, Xbox Ally X20, and select Windows Copilot Plus PCs, the company announced today.
body: With the official launch of Auto SR, your Xbox Ally X can use Microsoft’s upscaling technology undocked and with games running at 1080p.

In April, Microsoft started testing Auto SR on the Xbox Ally X, but you could only use it while docked. The full release of Auto SR announced today now works while you’re playing handheld and running on battery, and it also supports games running at 1080p. Microsoft does note that playing in handheld and at 1080p might lead to performance that “may not be as optimal as other configurations,” but says you’ll see visual improvements “especially in older games.”

Previously, Auto SR was also limited to framerates of “around” 60 to 75fps, but support for a new Auto SR Performance mode will allow you to hit framerates of up to 120fps. The Performance mode, and new compatibility with Auto HDR, will be available through Windows updates.

highlights.summary: Spoilers for VisionQuest and potentially Avengers: Doomsday are contained in the article below. You've been warned! The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.
body: Following the conclusion of VisionQuest, Marvel snuck in a little teaser for Avengers: Doomsday and/or Secret Wars during the credits. The scene was excluded from advanced screeners provided to the press, so it came as a big surprise and shows that Marvel made a great deal of effort to keep this moment a secret.

The show cut back to the ending of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, where Wanda Maximoff, AKA Scarlet Witch, uses her powers to destroy the Darkhold and, in the process, sacrifices herself. Her fate has remained unknown for over four years now, but now, we finally know what's next for her.

Doctor Doom shows up and lifts a bunch of rubble off of her, uttering the words: "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine." Her eyes open in shock before the scene cuts to black. The plot of Avengers: Doomsday has remained relatively abstract for some time now. Universes are starting to catastrophically collide as part of a series of "incursions," but the why and how of it all has remained a secret. Doom's larger plan and motive have also been kept under wraps, but we've started to get a better idea over the last couple of months.

highlights.title: Maybe it’s a new tagline. Maybe it’s more punctuation. Maybelline’s 35-year-old slogan has an update
highlights.summary: First introduced in 1991, ‘Maybe she’s born with it’ is out the door – but is the new slogan a glow-up? Alyx, I hear a certain makeup brand has updated its tagline. Why is this a big deal?
body: The jingle that has been burned into the minds of women around the world since its Christy Turlington-helmed debut in 1991, “Maybe she’s born with it, maybe it’s Maybelline”, has received what has being described as a “modernisation”. In a new campaign with Miley Cyrus, the “she’s” will be replaced with “we’re”, which both changes the observer’s perspective to something a little more self-directed and makes it more inclusive. But it’s a punctuation change that is raising eyebrows.
Replacing “she” with “we” feels like a positive move. So what’s turning heads?
They’ve replaced a single comma with a pair of full stops. The slogan is now: “Maybe. We’re born with it. Maybe. It’s Maybelline.”

Not according to Sandrine Jolly, global brand president of Maybelline New York. She told WWD that, previously, “the jingle was giving ambiguity – it was more of a question”. Now: “The ‘maybe’ is not a doubt or a hesitation any more. ‘Maybe’, period, is a statement of possibility, and that is what we want to be for women.”

highlights.title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
highlights.summary: The US military is taking a new approach to prop up commercial launch companies as SpaceX looks to wind down its Falcon rocket program, suggesting defense officials see the workhorse rocket's retirement as a potential national security risk.
body: The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital has twice in the last two weeks announced it was sending cash to two of SpaceX's competitors in the launch business. First, on October 26, the office announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space. Military officials revealed a second $150 million Pentagon loan Tuesday for Rocket Lab.

Stoke Space and Rocket Lab are the first two launch companies to receive significant support from the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), an organization established in 2022 to infuse companies developing "vital" national security technologies with capital. OSC has been on a loan spree in recent weeks, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to companies specializing in batteries, drones, and semiconductors. In the space sector, the office also provided a $150 million loan to LeoLabs, a commercial satellite tracking company, for production and deployment of radar units.

highlights.title: The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it
highlights.summary: As espionage targets go, Jensen Huang is perhaps one of the least surprising on Earth. The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world's most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people.
body: Nvidia’s chips are powering America’s AI boom. Of course Chinese spies are interested.

Which makes Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy — reportedly while her spying was known to US intelligence and even President Donald Trump — all the more shocking. The fallout goes well beyond his marriage, his reputation, or Nvidia itself. Experts tell The Verge the incident threatens to disrupt the entire US AI industry, potentially jeopardize national security, and could undermine America’s efforts to maintain its fragile technological lead over China in AI.
“With those chips, the US lead could vanish in a matter of weeks or months.”

highlights.title: Marvel's VisionQuest Series Finale Review: 'Forever'
highlights.summary: The last-minute addition of a new villain derails the finale of VisionQuest somewhat, but the series still succeeds where Vision and Ultron are concerned.
body: VisionQuest has certainly gained momentum with time, to the point where it easily ranks among the best of Marvel's live-action Disney+ shows to date (not that it looks like there's going to be much competition in the foreseeable future ). Sadly, that momentum doesn't entirely carry over into the final episode. "Forever" is a bit of a letdown compared to recent installments of the series, mainly due to the last-minute pivot to a new villain.

Part of it comes down to the notion that Ultron is based on a human model in the first place. The series lightly teased this a few episodes back when Ultron insisted to F.R.I.D.A.Y. that he was unique. Well, it turns out he isn't. It diminishes this villain a bit to see that all his acerbic, affected charm comes not from being invented in a lab by Tony Stark and immediately exposed to the horrors of the Internet, but because he's a copy of Jo Carrington's (T'Nia Miller) creepy ex-boyfriend. Ultimately, I might have been happier if the series had culminated with the more predictable reveal that Phineas Horton (Paul Bettany) or J.I.M. were the Client.

highlights.title: ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’
highlights.summary: ChatGPT is going to let you chat with verified "Business Agents" that represent a brand to help you with things like comparison shopping. The feature, available first to "eligible" e-commerce and online service businesses in the US, is launching as part of a suite of business-focused features in…
body: ChatGPT’s new AI agents represent companies and can help with things like comparison shopping.

You can start talking with a Business Agent if a business that has created one appears in a response from ChatGPT. While chatting with a custom agent, you can ask about a business’s offerings and ask follow-up questions, like asking about differences between two different products. Businesses can specify a Business Agent’s instructions and provide business context so that the agent knows how to respond.

Chats with Business Agents will be clearly labeled and separate from your main ChatGPT conversation, OpenAI says. To help people know that they’re talking with an agent that actually represents the business, companies will be able to claim their organization and get verified through a feature called Business Hub. (OpenAI isn’t sharing specifics about its verification methods because there are different methods for different businesses, VP of monetization Benji Shomair said in a press briefing.) Business Hub will also let companies see insights such as mentions in ChatGPT responses and top “discovery topics” where their business pops up.

body: The Czech, who beat Kostyuk in her opening match, has won both encounters without dropping a set and is assured of advancing to the knockout stage. Gauff and Pegula are both 1-1, with the final round-robin matches on Thursday set to determine who joins Noskova in the last four.
Pegula earlier bounced back from her opening defeat to Gauff with a 6-2, 7-5 victory over Kostyuk, eliminating the Ukrainian from semi-final contention.

The American made a strong start, breaking Kostyuk in the opening game and securing another break to claim the first set. She carried that momentum into the second, breaking again at the start before the pair exchanged breaks twice.
Kostyuk’s mistakes undermined her attempts to fight back, with the Ukrainian committing 17 unforced errors in the opening set compared with Pegula’s three.

highlights.title: Fortis Games Closes With Over 400 Jobs Impacted
highlights.summary: Fortis Games, a studio behind mobile titles like Twilight Towers and Bloom & Breakfast, has closed its doors, impacting around 440 jobs. CEO Steven Chiang confirmed the closure in a statement to GamesBeat on November 10, 2026.
body: “We have been fortunate to work with some of the most talented and dedicated people in this space. As we move forward, our primary focus will be on helping this talented team of individuals find new opportunities. Thank you to everyone who has supported us over the past five years. We are grateful for the collaboration and friendship we have shared with so many.”

Several former employees have spoken out about the closure in posts on LinkedIn. In one of these posts, game producer Gustavo Coronet confirmed that Las Vegas Sands Corp., Fortis Games’ parent company, chose to “end funding and part ways, terminating all of the contracts, worldwide.”

“Super proud of the work we’ve done. LVS’s decision does not delete the ground breaking and best-in class agentic development workflow the Octopus team has built, nor the massively solid soft launch metrics both our projects were achieving in such early stages of development,” he wrote.

In another post, former communications director Scott Butterworth suggested that Fortis’s “community-focused” approach to mobile games didn’t resonate enough with players to help it “get off the ground.”

highlights.title: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
highlights.summary: Amazon is betting that many Ring customers will also want an AI-powered security drone and robot patrolling their homes or offices. But the company’s upcoming Ring Robotic products are also certain to intensify privacy concerns previously raised around a prior Amazon attempt to popularize a flying…
body: The Ring Rover Cam and Ring Drone Cam are expected to reach customers starting at the end of 2026 and in early 2027, respectively, according to an Amazon announcement posted on November 10. Amazon describes the devices as relying on an AI Pilot system that uses each device’s cameras along with “specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing” to plan patrol routes while autonomously navigating around obstacles such as furniture.

Both devices also use that AI Pilot system to digitally map the floor plan of the customer’s home or business. This setup process occurs after the customer carries the Ring drone through their indoor spaces or allows the Ring Rover to do some autonomous exploration.

The AI Pilot can supposedly use that guided- or self-tour information to identify specific rooms and suggest patrol points near side doors, windows, or even sensitive locations such as a cash register in the case of a business.

However, flying and roving cameras with AI-enabled features could introduce new privacy risks for homes and businesses, on top of existing concerns involving fixed Ring cameras installed in room corners or as doorbell cameras.

body: OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson. Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire. Davidson’s announcement focused largely on how he built his AI travel agent Odessia by directing teams of AI agents. The year-old Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent around five months ago. Davidson says that it had helped early adopters plan millions of dollars’ worth of travel, but the tool has already been shut down.

An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the hire to TechCrunch. “We’re thrilled to welcome Francis to OpenAI. Francis is a proven founder who has built multiple businesses to help people travel, and we’re excited he’s chosen to build with us.”

highlights.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
highlights.summary: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.
body: New York is gearing up to enforce one of the country’s most significant AI safety laws. The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027.

The RAISE Act, New York’s safety and transparency bill, kicks in at the start of the year. It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports.

The newly formed Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will implement the RAISE Act and oversee large frontier AI labs. Penalties can be as high as $1 million for one violation and $3 million for subsequent violations.
The state also can bring enforcement actions against companies that fail to register with the new portal, though a spokesperson declined to provide specifics.
points: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, requiring major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.

While it's not quite as difficult as the 1998 PlayStation original, FF Tactics demands that you engage deeply with its job system and figure out which team compositions are necessary for a specific battle.
